title: circle_channels is readable by anyone with the anon key, so it lists the ids of hidden Circles
detail: FOUND 2026-10-05 in the scan-six read of LIVE-666 (c8055a7, migration 20270345011400). The select policy is `using (true)` with select granted to anon and authenticated. An unlisted, closed Circle is meant to be invisible to anyone who cannot enter it (ADR-1015, circles_access_restrictive); `select * from circle_channels` over PostgREST returns every hidden Circle's uuid and the Channels it carries. NOT a plain revoke: scripts/table-grants.txt records that the signed-out Circles index embeds circle_channels on the session client, so revoking breaks that embed. THE FIX: replace the policy with `using (exists (select 1 from public.circles c where c.id = circle_id))` so it inherits the circles RLS, prove it on the db-tests database (signed-out index still lists public Circles' Channels; a hidden Circle's row is absent for anon), then apply and reconcile the ledger version.

source.ref: found 2026-10-05 by the scan-six adversarial read of the 2026-09-28..30 merges
